title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
author: Elijah Newren
description: Git is releasing updates addressing six security vulnerabilities affecting recursive clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports. Here is what users need to know. The post Git security vulnerabilities announced appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
summary: Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when recursively cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches.
takeaways: We are coordinating releases of GitHub Desktop and the GitHub Copilot app that include patched versions of Git.
We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git.

The release also validates other reference names and symbolic-reference targets received through protocol v2. [ Advisory ] CVE-2026-114467: Stack corruption when removing signatures When stripping GPG signatures from a message, Git assumed there would be at most two signatures.
